title: Business & Management: from analysis to action

groups.description: Understand the choices, assumptions and levels of strategy.

groups.name: Markets & competition
groups.description: Read the environment, identify rivals and choose a position.

groups.name: Resources & advantage
groups.description: Examine the capabilities, networks and activities behind customer value.

groups.name: Growth & innovation
groups.description: Explore new products, markets and ways to develop the business.

groups.name: Decisions & execution
groups.description: Evaluate options, allocate resources and measure progress.

groups.name: Leadership & organizational change
groups.description: Build teams and support the organizational work of change.

groups.name: Sales & customer relationships
groups.description: Find fit, discover needs, agree decisions and support customers.

groups.description: Plan revenue, coordinate accounts and coach the sales organization.

groups.name: Negotiation
groups.description: Prepare, create options and reach workable agreements.

groups.name: Productivity & priorities
groups.description: Turn goals into focused work and a manageable workflow.

groups.name: Strategy classics
groups.description: Read historical strategy with clearly separated modern reflections.

notes: Supplied examples, claims and checklists accompany the summaries. Incomplete entries and uncertain claims are identified on their relevant pages.
Historical company examples and numerical sales claims are study material, not verified current benchmarks. Original diagrams are rebuilt as readable visuals; unavailable content is disclosed.

title: Communication & Personal Development
summary: Explore listening, clear expression, persuasion and the supplied NLP reference material with context and evidence notes.
intro: Start with practical communication, then explore the reference collection while distinguishing source claims from established evidence.

groups.name: Communication & influence
groups.description: Listen, explain and discuss value with clarity and respect.

groups.name: Learning & personal development
groups.description: Examine learning and creative-thinking material, including incomplete exercises.

groups.name: NLP reference
groups.description: Read the source terminology as an annotated reference, with evidence and scope notes.

notes: NLP in this collection means neuro-linguistic programming, distinct from natural language processing in AI.
Language and personality labels are descriptions from the collection, not diagnoses or fixed categories for judging people. Therapeutic claims are separated and discussed critically.

title: Sales playbook: from prospecting to customer success
summary: Follow the buyer journey, prepare conversations and explore the work of leading a sales team.
intro: Use the journey for a live opportunity or browse the detailed guides for a question you need to answer.

groups.name: Sales & customer relationships
groups.description: Find fit, prepare questions, address concerns and support the customer.

groups.name: Sales leadership & operations
groups.description: Plan, forecast, coordinate accounts and coach the team.

notes: Use the question bank flexibly rather than as a script. Respect a buyer’s refusal, preferences and confidentiality.
Unreferenced statistics and questionable influence anecdotes are retained with reading notes, not promoted as facts or recommended tactics.

title: Neuro-linguistic programming: an annotated reference
summary: Explore the supplied language patterns, perspectives, sorting terms and development claims without confusing descriptions with validated methods.
intro: This reference preserves the collection’s definitions and examples. It distinguishes communication prompts, mixed personality terminology, metaphors and therapeutic claims.

groups.name: NLP language & communication
groups.description: Read the language-pattern examples and communication stances.

groups.name: NLP perspectives & preferences
groups.description: Explore perspectives and sorting terminology without treating labels as fixed traits.

groups.name: Learning & personal development
groups.description: Inspect the learning descriptions and the scope of development claims.

links.label: Read the evidence and therapeutic-claim notes

notes: The collection’s warning against rigid labels remains part of the reading path.
The 2012 Sturt et al. review reported limited evidence for NLP health outcomes and emphasized the quantity and quality of the research. It is not an evaluation of every term in this glossary.
The descriptions of trauma, addiction, eating and reprocessing methods are retained as source claims, not supplied as treatment instructions.

references.title: Sturt et al. (2012): systematic review of NLP health outcomes

title: The Art of War: a guided reading collection
summary: Read all thirteen supplied chapters, with concise introductions and clearly separated business reflections.
intro: Read in chapter order or choose a theme. The historical text remains accessible in full; the modern reflections are editorial additions, not claims made by the original author.

groups.name: Strategy classics
groups.description: All thirteen supplied chapters, in reading order.

notes: This is historical military writing. Its descriptions of violence, deception and coercion are retained in context, not turned into business recommendations.

The supplied document does not name its translation or edition. A separate Lionel Giles edition is linked for comparison. Repeated passages are consolidated without removing unique content, and source positions remain mapped.

references.title: Project Gutenberg: Lionel Giles translation (comparison edition)

title: Project Management: plan, deliver and improve
summary: Explore planning, delivery, Six Sigma, risk, measurement and team responsibilities through connected guides.
intro: Start with a project question or browse the six sections. Six Sigma & Process Improvement is a focused collection within this wider project-management hub.

groups.name: Planning & governance
groups.description: Clarify scope, objectives, ownership, selection and review.

groups.name: Delivery approaches
groups.description: Compare software delivery methods, assumptions and feedback loops.

groups.name: Six Sigma & process improvement
groups.description: Explore variation, DMAIC/DMADV, robust design and operational improvement.

groups.name: Risk & assurance
groups.description: Examine analytical questions, evidence, failure modes and safety-study limitations.

groups.name: Estimation & performance
groups.description: Read estimation, measurement, size-accounting and tracking references.

groups.name: Teams, responsibilities & change
groups.description: Clarify responsibilities, organizational context and the human work of change.

notes: This collection currently emphasizes process improvement, safety/risk analysis and software delivery. The hierarchy can grow with additional project-management material.
Six Sigma is placed here as an improvement approach. Its use in ongoing operations is also connected through Business & Management.
Missing figures, incomplete templates and inconsistent source calculations are disclosed on the relevant pages; no missing project data are invented.

title: Six Sigma & Process Improvement
summary: Explore variation, Lean, DMAIC/DMADV, robust design and process architecture within Project Management.
intro: Use this focused collection for improvement work, then return to Project Management for governance, delivery, risk, people and performance.

groups.name: Six Sigma & process improvement
groups.description: Read the fundamentals and tools together with their source limitations.

notes: The parent is Project Management. Process-improvement methods also apply to ongoing operations and are cross-linked from the business collection.
The supplied material mixes historical descriptions, named frameworks and incomplete technical examples. A method name or diagram does not constitute a completed improvement project.

title: Technology: software, models and systems

notes: Technical models are classified by what they describe; they are not all treated as Six Sigma methods or project-management frameworks.
Existing technical articles retain their URLs and content. Historical tools and incomplete abstracts carry their own source notes.
